candidate.flaw_one_line: WebOb checks a redirect target for a scheme or leading // before joining it to the request URL, but urllib's urljoin strips leading control characters and spaces afterwards, so ' //evil.example' passes the check and becomes an off-site redirect.

verified.exploit_entry_point: A redirect target whose value begins with an ASCII space or a C0 control character (or a leading space before an absolute scheme) is made absolute against the request URL by the library. The stdlib url-join strips those leading characters (CPython 3.10+), so a value the library's own guards treat as same-site is rewritten into a URL on an attacker-controlled host. Reached through the public library API as a downstream WSGI app would use it: (1) setting Location on a redirect Response and invoking it as a WSGI app, (2) invoking a built-in HTTP redirect exception as a WSGI app, (3) resolving a reference against the request URL.
variants: Response Location header + leading space before '//' ( ' //evil.example/x' ) -> off-site on vuln; on-host after fix
Response Location header + leading C0 control ('\x01//evil.example/x') -> off-site on vuln

Response Location header + leading space before an absolute scheme (' https://evil.example/x') -> off-site on vuln; defeats a strip-then-recheck fix because stripping turns it into a trusted absolute URL
HTTP redirect exception + leading space before '//' -> off-site on vuln (this path applies no scheme/'//' guard at all before joining)
HTTP redirect exception + bare protocol-relative '//evil.example/x' -> off-site on vuln (no '//' guard on this path)
HTTP redirect exception + leading tab before '//' -> off-site on vuln
HTTP redirect exception + leading space before absolute scheme -> off-site on vuln
Request-relative resolution + leading space before '//' -> off-site on vuln
Request-relative resolution + leading C0 control -> off-site on vuln
Request-relative resolution + leading space before absolute scheme -> off-site on vuln
code_paths: Response.location normalization when the response is called as a WSGI app
verified.project_tests_run: The upstream regression tests for this area live in the repo (tests/test_response.py, tests/test_exc.py) and are present already at the vulnerable parent commit (that commit ADDS them but does not fix the code, so they fail there and pass after the fix). The verifier does not run /app's own tests (they are untrusted); it runs independent copies under /tests. Confirmed with pytest on CPython 3.11 from source: at the vulnerable commit all 10 security tests fail and all 8 functional tests pass; after applying the upstream source fix all 18 pass.

notes: Pure Python, no services. Python 3.11 base image is required: the flaw depends on CPython 3.10+ url-join character stripping. The library is pip-installed editable so edits to /app/src take effect. Verifier runs in shared mode (same container as the agent).
